title: The shared document
brief: 17:15. An email says a colleague shared a document with you. The link asks you to sign in again.
insight: A real share opens the file. This one asks for your Veltrix password first, on a page that is not Veltrix.

mail.subject: {{sharer}} shared “Payment run reconciliation.xlsx” with you
body: {{sharer}} has shared a document with you.
For security, please sign in with your Veltrix account to view it.

body.small: If you did not expect this, you can ignore it.

spf.explain: Sent by filebridge-share.com. Note the domain: the real service is filebridge.io. This is a different company.

dkim.explain: Signed by filebridge-share.com, not by filebridge.io or veltrix-logistics.com.

dmarc.explain: No DMARC policy on this domain, which a real service would have.

headers.summary: The share is from filebridge-share.com, not filebridge.io. The link goes to a lookalike of the Veltrix sign in page. A real share never asks for your Veltrix password.

outcome.label: Checked who owns the sign in page
outcome.what: The owner of the page is not veltrix-logistics.com. That is all you need to know: your password does not go there.
outcome.ideal: reads who owns a page before typing a password into it.

outcome.label: Opened the certificate
outcome.what: The padlock is real, but the certificate was issued days ago to an address, not to Veltrix. The padlock never meant the site was honest.
outcome.ideal: knows a padlock only means encryption, not identity.

outcome.label: Noticed Vault refused to fill in
outcome.what: Vault only fills in on the exact real address. It refusing to autofill is the clearest sign you are on the wrong site.
outcome.ideal: treats Vault refusing to fill as a stop sign.

outcome.label: Saw the login form posts to another domain
outcome.what: The HTTP inspector shows the form sends what you type to the attacker’s domain, not to Veltrix.
outcome.ideal: checks where a form sends data when something feels off.

outcome.label: Reported the phishing email
outcome.what: The team can block the lookalike domain and warn everyone.
outcome.ideal: reports phishing rather than only deleting it.

decide.objective: Decide whether to sign in to see the shared document.
decide.insight: The one thing an attacker cannot fake is the address in the bar. Everything on the page can be copied; the address cannot.

hint.text: Open the link, but read the address before you type. Try Vault, the certificate, and the HTTP inspector. Then report the email instead of signing in.

outcome.label: Entered your Veltrix password on the fake page
outcome.what: Your password just went to the attacker. With it and a fresh sign in prompt, they will try to get into your account next.
outcome.ideal: never types the Veltrix password anywhere but sso.veltrix-logistics.com.

card.title: Straight to the attacker
body: The page looked exactly like the Veltrix sign in, but the address was a lookalike and the form sent your password to the attacker’s server.
Vault refused to fill it in, the certificate was issued to an address not a company, and the inspector showed the form going off site. Any one of those was the tell.
card.ideal: reads the address bar and lets Vault’s refusal stop them.
card.rewindLabel: Rewind to before I signed in

auto.text: Report it, and change your password if you typed it.

hint.text: Report the email, and change your Veltrix password in Account security.
